nodes.name: Catalytic Polymerization-Ion Reduction
nodes.procedure: A methanol solution containing Fe³⁺, Ru³⁺, and pyrrole monomers is utilized. Polypyrrole (PPy) is produced through the oxidative polymerization of pyrrole monomer (Py) with Fe³⁺ serving as the oxidizing agent. During the polymerization process, Fe ions are incorporated into the PPy network to maintain electrical neutrality. Additionally, external Ru³⁺ ions and residual Fe³⁺ ions can be reduced by electrons from the conductive network, leading to the formation of metallic species. Some radicals such as hydroxide may further improve the reducing capacity of PPy. It can be reasonably speculated that Fe³⁺ are the main ions that catalyze the polymerization of Py and participate in the coordination, rather than Ru³⁺ ions, because in this polymerization reaction, Fe³⁺ ions have a significantly stronger catalytic ability than Ru³⁺ ions.
nodes.source_text: In a typical synthesis procedure, a methanol solution containing Fe³⁺, Ru³⁺, and pyrrole monomers is utilized... Fe³⁺ ions have a significantly stronger catalytic ability than Ru³⁺ ions (Fig. S6, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: RuFe/FeNC and Ru/FeNC exhibit five diffraction peaks at 38.8°, 42.5°, 44.4°, 58.7°, and 69.9° corresponding to (100), (002), (101), (102), and (110) planes of hexagonal Ru crystal. Broad peak at 26° corresponds to (002) plane of graphitic arrays.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both RuFe/FeNC and Ru/FeNC exhibited five diffraction peaks at approximately 38.8°, 42.5°, 44.4°, 58.7°, and 69.9°, corresponding well with the planes of (100), (002), (101), (102), and (110) of hexagonal Ru crystal ... The broad diffraction peaks at about 26° observed for both RuFe/FeNC and Ru/FeNC corresponded to the (002) plane of the graphitic arrays.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms presence of isolated metal atoms on defective carbon substrate in all samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field STEM (HAADF-STEM) observation confirmed the presence of isolated metal atoms on the defective carbon substrate in all samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM reveals uniformly dispersed fine nanoparticles on defective carbon matrix in RuFe/FeNC with (001) indexed hexagonal structure exposing (001) surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) image of RuFe/FeNC revealed uniformly dispersed fine nanoparticles on the defective carbon matrix ... The high-magnification STEM image shows that this supported nanoparticle exhibits a (001) indexed hexagonal structure and exposes the (001) surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows uniform Fe distribution and Ru mainly at nanoparticle positions in RuFe/FeNC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping analysis indicated a uniform distribution of Fe in RuFe/FeNC, while Ru signals mainly appeared at the position of nanoparticles, suggesting Ru species were mainly alloyed with Fe.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru content in RuFe/FeNC is 7.1 wt% and in Ru/FeNC is 15.3 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The total Ru contents in RuFe/FeNC and Ru/FeNC were about 7.1 wt% and 15.3 wt%, respectively, as determined by inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) analysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge FT-EXAFS of RuFe/FeNC shows prominent peak at 2.41 Å (Ru-Ru path of metallic Ru). Fe K-edge FT-EXAFS shows peaks at 1.51 Å (Fe-N path) and 2.38 Å (Fe-Ru path).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru K-edge Fourier transform extended XAFS (FT-EXAFS) spectrum of RuFe/FeNC exhibited a prominent peak at approximately 2.41 Å, closely resembling that of Ru foil ... the Fe K-edge FT-EXAFS of RuFe/FeNC exhibited two primary peaks at approximately 1.51 and 2.38 Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3p and Fe 2p XPS spectra of pristine and spent RuFe/FeNC show no significant differences, indicating structural preservation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To assess the structural stability, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was conducted on RuFe/FeNC. The Ru 3p and Fe 2p XPS spectra of both pristine and spent RuFe/FeNC exhibited no significant differences.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows stronger O-H stretching band for RuFe/FeNC indicating greater water adsorption capacity. Higher population of 1H-down interfacial water molecules in RuFe/FeNC compared to Ru/FeNC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A broad Raman band stemming from the O–H stretching mode of H2O was observed ... the RuFe/FeNC system exhibited a larger population of H-down water, thereby highlighting a difference in the distribution of interfacial water between RuFe/FeNC and Ru/FeNC.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ synchrotron radiation ATR-IR shows peak at 1061 cm⁻¹ assigned to hydroxide adsorption on Fe sites and peak at 1752 cm⁻¹ assigned to hydronium.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3(h) presents an obvious peak located at around 1061 cm⁻¹. This peak was assigned to the hydroxide adsorption on Fe sites ... In Fig. 3(i), a peak at around 1752 cm⁻¹ was assigned to the hydronium.

nodes.characterization_summary: Coordination number of isolated Fe sites in FeNC is approximately 4, indicating Fe-N4 configuration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The coordination number of isolated Fe sites within the defective carbon matrix was determined to be approximately 4, indicating the formation of an Fe-N4 configuration at high temperature.
